slides.title: Network Protocols
content: Network protocols are standardized rules that define how data is transmitted, received, structured, and processed between devices in a network
They ensure reliable communication, proper sequencing, and error handling during data exchange
Protocols enable interoperability between different devices, systems, and vendors across global networks
They support scalability, security, and efficient troubleshooting in modern networking systems

slides.title: Types of Network Protocols
content: Communication protocols like HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, IMAP, and POP3 are used for data exchange between applications
Transport protocols like TCP and UDP manage end-to-end data transmission between devices
Routing protocols like OSPF and BGP determine optimal paths for data across networks
Security protocols like SSL/TLS and IPSec provide encryption and authentication for secure communication

slides.title: TCP Protocol
content: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable and ordered delivery of data
It establishes a connection using a three-way handshake before data transmission begins
It performs error detection, retransmission of lost packets, and flow and congestion control
It is used in applications like web browsing (HTTP/HTTPS), email (SMTP), and file transfer (FTP)

slides.title: UDP Protocol
content: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a connectionless protocol that focuses on fast and low-latency data transmission
It does not guarantee delivery, order, or error correction of packets
It has low overhead and sends data as independent datagrams without establishing a connection
It is used in real-time applications like video streaming, online gaming, and VoIP communication

slides.title: Application Layer Protocols
content: Application layer protocols enable communication between user applications and the network by providing services like web browsing, email, and file transfer
HTTP and HTTPS are used for web communication where HTTPS provides secure encrypted transmission using SSL/TLS
FTP is used for file transfer between client and server, while SMTP is used for sending emails
SNMP is used for monitoring and managing network devices like routers and switches

slides.title: Network Layer Functions & Protocols
content: The network layer provides logical addressing using IP addresses and enables communication between different networks
Routing determines the best path for data transmission using algorithms and routing protocols
Packet forwarding transfers data packets across networks using routing tables
Protocols like IP (IPv4, IPv6), ICMP, ARP, and BGP handle addressing, error reporting, and routing operations
